Pause on P-sciml for a complete evidence
reading of Experiment

P — sin-dee scientific pipeline ordering.
First, identify the research

question before looking at the answer. The
question asks whether

the fixed components create a meaningful
ordering surface, whether a

particular neighborhood provides useful
guidance on that surface, or whether

a cheaper executor is equally effective.
The sample is All
720 orderings, and the source artifact is

experiments/iteration-16/results/sciml_landscape.csv.
The horizontal axis

names the recorded independent
quantity—such as permutation size,

distance, or distinct evaluations. The
vertical axis names the measured

outcome—such as accuracy, error, hit
probability, regret, correlation, or

hitting time. Raw points remain visible
when their count permits.

A summary line or bar describes those
points; it does

not replace them. A capped observation
receives a censor marker,

and a sampled landscape never pretends to
be exhaustively enumerated.

The central pattern supports this finding:
Result: recovery error ranged

from 0.1% to 23.2% by ordering alone. The
correct limitation

is: The conclusion is scoped to the
recorded evaluator, landscape,

and budget. That limitation rules out a
broader promotional interpretation

while preserving the result actually
measured. The decision carried into

the research program is: Pre-flight: F D C
+0.109, treated

as borderline under Decision D19. Finally,
compare against the equal-budget

alternative. Generations, repeated cache
hits, and distinct evaluations are

not interchangeable. A method earns a
search-efficiency claim only when

uncertainty, evaluator resolution, optimum
density, and evaluation cost have
all been accounted for.
